newsitem.title: UK: Oil price eases as U.S. inventories rise.
newsitem.headline: Oil price eases as U.S. inventories rise.

text.p: Oil prices teetered from their highs on Friday despite Europe's big freeze as traders decided a rise in U.S. inventories was reason enough to take profits.
London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent blend dipped 30 cents to $23.93 a barrel at 1530 GMT.
Traders said a bigger than expected build in U.S. distillates stocks, comprising heating oil and diesel, had undermined prices because dealers were expecting only a modest rise in inventories.
"The U.S. inventory data has given people the opportunity to take some profits," said a trader in London.

The American Petroleum Institute said U.S. distillates stocks in the week to December 27 rose 2.47 million barrels while the government's Energy Information Administration said stocks rose 4.1 million barrels.
"Distillate stocks are only 5.4 million barrels below a year ago now, so barring any real prolonged cold spell, it looks bearish," said Victor Yu, vice president of brokers Refco in New York.
Market weakness was exacerbated by forecasts for continued mild weather in the U.S. northeast, the world's single largest heating oil consuming region.
But dealers said expectations that Europe's New Year freeze would continue into next week would prevent prices slumping too heavily.
"A severe cold wave continues as the predominant wind flow is from the east. Energy demand has been and will continue to be well above normal," said U.S. Weather Services Corp.
Some waterways which take heating oil up the river Rhine to the important German market were partially blocked by ice early on Thursday and likely to cause delays, traders said.

Germany, easily Europe's biggest heating oil consumer, has been running on unusually thin inventories. German household stocks of heating oil fell in November to about 62 percent of capacity from 68 percent last year, traders estimate. Crude oil prices in dollars per barrel:
